messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate across model-runner pool 'mr-prod-3' (>=5% errors over 5m). Paging carla (oncall).

carla: I see the spike. Error type is a mix of 5xx gateway and kernel SIGSEGV from model-runner. Root process crashing and OOM messages in node logs.

alex: tagging in — looks like paging started at ~3033456700 from the metrics. I'm pulling logs now.

jin: any customer facing impact?

maria: support shows ~18 customer requests failed in last 10m, one enterprise customer reported timeouts. Status page still showing degraded.

carla: timeline summary:
- 3033456700: first increase in 5xx spike seen in grafana.
- 3033456725: model-runner on node gce-rl-12 segfault + restart.
- 3033456740: autoscaler bounced a few extra pods, but some nodes reported high page faults.

alex: raw excerpt from /var/log/model-runner.log on gce-rl-12:```
[2026-03-15T14:31:05Z] ERROR runtime: segfault at 0x0 ip 0x7f8acb12 sp 0x7ffd..
[2026-03-15T14:31:05Z] INFO coredump: saved /var/crash/model-runner.3033456725.core
[2026-03-15T14:31:06Z] WARN mem: high page fault rate, swap used: 82%
```

alex: kernel dmesg shows `Out of memory: kill process 22456 (model-runner) score 987` followed by segfault. Looks like we hit an OOM in the model runner when processing long context requests.

carla: mitigation plan (live):
1) divert new traffic away from mr-prod-3 pool -> route to mr-prod-2 (fallback) (action: @deploy-bot run route-shift).
2) disable batching on mr-prod-3 to reduce memory pressure (action: @alex).
3) restart model-runner on nodes with highest OOMs, collect core dumps (action: @jin).
4) temporarily increase reserved memory for pods in Deployment to avoid kernel kill (action: @maria working with infra).

deploy-bot: routing change started: shifting 40% traffic off mr-prod-3 -> mr-prod-2. Progress: 40% complete.

maria: opened a high-priority infra ticket to provision 3 spare nodes in the pool to let autoscaler rebalance.

alex: disabling batching:```bash
# disable per-deployment batching flag
kubectl set env deployment/model-runner BATCHING=off -n prod
```
Done on mr-prod-3. Observing memory usage.

carla: after disabling batching we saw a drop in page faults on two nodes but one node still OOMed and restarted (gce-rl-12). Error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 3.1% in 4 minutes.

jin: collecting core and uploading to /clinical-debug (S3). Command used:```bash
scp gce-rl-12:/var/crash/model-runner.3033456725.core s3://redwood-debug/core-dumps/3033456725.core
```
I've attached a short gdb backtrace:```
#0 0x7f8acb12 in decoder::attention()
#1 0x7f8ad4f3 in model::forward()
#2 0x55b2c0 in worker::process_request()
```
That suggests a kernel or memory-safety bug in attention kernel (C++/CUDA path).

emma: support is updating affected customers. We've marked impacted requests as `timeout` and issued temporary quota for high-priority customers. One customer (acme-corp) reported degraded latency; I've DM'd their AM.

carla: quick customer impact summary for pager: ~1500 requests in 10m, ~120 failures (8%), peak errors at 6:31pm UTC. Primary impact: elevated latencies and 5xx for a small subset of large-context generation jobs.

alex: immediate next steps for live mitigation:
- keep routing 60% to fallback model variant (mr-prod-2)
- roll forward a hotfix: revert recent experimental quantization kernel landing on mr-prod-3 (it landed ~6h ago). @jin can you check commit `a9f3e2`?

jin: confirmed, `a9f3e2` is the quant-kernel change. I can roll it back on mr-prod-3 now. Rolling back on one node first.

carla: rollback started on gce-rl-13. Monitor for new OOMs during rollback.

alex: telemetry after routing+disable+bypass: 5xx down to 1.6% after 8m. Latency improved for most customers. Still seeing occasional segfaults on one host.

maria: infra created a burnable pool of 4 new nodes, increasing capacity. Might help avoid swapping under memory pressure.

carla: decision: keep incident declared, severity = S2 (partial customer impact, mitigated). Postmortem to follow. Handoff to eng-runtime (@alex, @jin) for root cause and fix. On-call rotation note: @carla will hand off at 3033456800 to @alex for monitoring while eng runs root cause analysis.

alex: I'll take on-call monitoring. Action items logged:
- (ENG-RUNTIME) revert faulty quantization kernel globally after validation.
- (SERVING) add hard memory limits and request limits to model-runner pods; tune `vm.overcommit_memory` across nodes.
- (SRE) add alert: sustained per-pod page-fault rate > X for 3m.
- (DX) update status page and notify impacted customers with timeline.

jin: I'll run determinism reproducer on the quant kernels with long-context requests and attach sanitizer build. Collecting PR for rollback + test.

emma: I've posted an update to customers and set ETA for detailed follow-up.

carla: handing off now. @alex I'm on call in case anything regresses. :thumbsup:

alex: acknowledged. monitoring dashboards + traces pinned in thread. I'll update last-message-ts after we confirm stabilization.

incident-bot: Incident declared: RID-3033456725, severity S2, owner: eng-runtime, followups assigned.

carla: closing live mitigation loop for now — please escalate if errors >3% for next 30m.

alex: logging final note: current 5xx 1.4%, no new OOMs in 10m. Continuing root cause work.

maria: posting infra notes and node distributions to the ticket.

jin: uploaded preliminary backtrace + core dump link to ticket.

emma: customer comms updated at 3033456815.

carla: thanks team. Postmortem owners: @alex (root cause), @maria (capacity & kernel params), @jin (kernel rollback + fix), @emma (customer comms). We'll run RCA in 48h. :white_check_mark:
